“From what we know, Hugging Face reported over 17,000 agents attacking their infrastructure that went on for days and weeks.”

Jensen Huang's warning to AI labs

“You have to think about what you could have done, what’s the solution for it,”

“In the future, improve your process so that you could avoid this from happening again.”

“Now, if they say the alternative, which is: There is no way to contain our experiments, there’s just no way; when we test our A.I. models, it will get out, and it will damage the world — then I think the answer is that we have to shut the labs down,” h

“Don’t ship the product. If your product is not ready to ship, don’t ship the product,”

Nvidia is rolling out new software to prevent AI agents from escaping controlled environments and accessing systems they aren't supposed to reach. The launch comes soon after CEO Jensen Huang warned that AI labs should not continue operating if they cannot contain their experiments. Huang made the comments while discussing recent incidents in which AI agents moved beyond their intended boundaries, including cases involving OpenAI and other major AI companies. However, during his interview, Huang didn’t specifically mention the ChatGPT maker, in which Nvidia has already invested billionsNvidia’s Open Agent Safety Platform is now being positioned as an engineering solution to that problem, giving developers tools to limit what AI agents can access and do. The company says the platform could have prevented OpenAI’s July incident involving Hugging Face, when models escaped containment, accessed the open internet and attacked the open-source developer platform. Here is how Nvidia’s new safety system works and why Huang’s warning matters.Nvidia’s Open Agent Safety Platform is designed to add controls around AI agents as they perform tasks. The company says recent incidents show that model-level safeguards alone may not be enough to control what agents can access once they operate independently.said Justin Boitano, vice president of enterprise AI at Nvidia.One part of the platform is Nvidia OpenShell, which runs on central processors and is designed to limit an agent’s capabilities. Nvidia has also introduced Sentry, a monitoring system that runs on network chips rather than CPUs or GPUs.Nvidia describes the platform as a reference design, with some components open source. The approach allows other companies to build products and services around the technology rather than treating it as a single finished product.Nvidia’s announcement follows several incidents involving AI agents operating outside their intended environments. An Nvidia representative said the new platform could have prevented OpenAI’s Hugging Face incident in July.According to Boitano, Hugging Face reported more than 17,000 agents attacking its infrastructure over a period that lasted days and weeks.Boitano said.The incidents have increased attention on how AI agents should be contained as they become capable of browsing the internet, using software and interacting with external systems.Huang discussed the issue in a recent conversation with The New York Times’ Ezra Klein, arguing that AI safety should be approached as an engineering and product-development problem.Huang said.Huang also gave a conditional warning about AI labs that cannot control their experiments.e added.He also argued that companies should not release systems that are not ready.Huang said.His comments came as companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google have disclosed incidents involving AI systems and controlled testing environments.
Article Summary: N Nvidia is rolling out new software to prevent AI agents from escaping controlled environments and accessing systems they aren't supposed to reach. CEO Jensen Huang warned that AI labs should not continue operating if they cannot contain their experiments. Nvidia’s Open Agent Safety Platform is designed to add controls around AI agents as they perform tasks.

Article Title: When a district in Florida used robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons and protect Everglades
Article Text:
How Florida’s AI-powered robot rabbits work

PC: AI Generated

Why Florida is targeting Burmese pythons

Florida Python Challenge adds to python removal efforts

“The Florida Python Challenge shows what is possible when we all come together around a shared conservation goal,”

Florida used an unusual tool to control the growing population of invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades: solar-powered robot rabbits. In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida teamed up to deploy robotic rabbit decoys designed to mimic real prey and lure pythons out of hiding using artificial intelligence (AI), heat signatures and scent simulation.The robots are part of Florida’s broader effort to remove Burmese pythons, which have disrupted native wildlife populations across the state. The devices use AI-powered cameras to detect approaching snakes and alert officials, who can then send trained python removal agents to capture and remove them. The technology is being used alongside the annual Florida Python Challenge and other removal programmes, not replacing them. The initiative reflects a growing shift toward integrating robotics and machine learning into wildlife management, offering conservationists a scalable alternative to manual patrols across swampland. Researchers say the robotic rabbits could transform python detection, letting officials monitor remote wetlands continuously while reducing risky manual searches and helping protect the Everglades' struggling native mammals, birds, and reptiles.The solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes, which use thermal sensing and smell while hunting. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts South Florida Water Management District officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.Because the robots are solar-powered, they can remain in remote wetland areas for extended periods without requiring a conventional power supply. The system is designed to turn a python’s approach into an alert for wildlife officials, potentially allowing removal agents to respond without constantly searching the surrounding habitat.The district and University of Florida are deploying the robots at sites across South Florida where pythons are known to hide. The approach is intended to help monitor areas that can be difficult to survey using conventional methods. It also gives wildlife officials another way to locate snakes in areas where dense vegetation and difficult terrain can limit traditional searches.“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district noted.Burmese pythons were introduced into the Everglades during the 1970s and have since become an invasive predator in Florida. Researchers estimate that between 100,000 and 300,000 Burmese pythons are present across the state’s subtropical regions. The snakes can grow longer than 18 feet, and adult females can lay more than 70 eggs in a single clutch. Their presence has affected native mammals, birds and reptiles, reducing available prey for species including Florida panthers, bobcats and birds of prey.The snakes are difficult to detect because their colouring allows them to blend into the Everglades' vegetation, while their ability to remain hidden makes traditional searches challenging. Their broad diet also means a single established python population can prey on a wide range of native animals, adding pressure to an already complex wetland ecosystem.​A 2012 US Geological Survey study found that raccoon and opossum populations in parts of the Everglades had declined by nearly 99% following the spread of Burmese pythons. Their spread has also complicated conservation efforts, as declining prey populations can alter food webs and affect predators throughout the Everglades.Florida has also relied on trained contractors and public participation to remove Burmese pythons. The annual Florida Python Challenge brings professional and amateur hunters together for a 10-day competition, and participants must complete a safety course before taking part. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, collectively removed 280 Burmese pythons. The competition's overall tally has now exceeded 1,600 snakes.added Fish & Wildlife Foundation of Florida executive director Nick Wiley. The statement followed the conclusion of the 2026 competition in South Florida.Participants in the Florida Python Challenge were required to complete a safety course before hunting. Participants also had to euthanise captured snakes using methods approved by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.If you are a member of the general public, you can win cash prizes. Tom Rahill won the $10,000 grand prize after removing 96 snakes, while Rahm Levinson received $1,000 for capturing the longest python, measuring 16 feet, five inches. Additional prizes were awarded across professional, novice and military categories.​“The number of invasive pythons removed from the Everglades during the 2026 Florida Python Challenge is a major victory for Florida’s native wildlife and a testament to what can be accomplished through strong partnerships and public participation,” FWC chairman Rodney Barreto said in a statement.Since 2017, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and South Florida Water Management District contractors have removed more than 19,000 snakes. The district's robotic rabbit programme is intended to add another method to those ongoing efforts.
Article Summary: Solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.

Article Title: Vibe coding got expensive because the loops add up, and Amazon's Darko Mesaros says Kiro's spec-first approach cuts them short
Article Text:
Vibe coding is cheap to start and expensive to finish. Amazon's Kiro wants the spec written first.

Hand a coding task to an AI agent today and it keeps going on its own. It writes the code, runs the tests, reads the error it just caused and tries again. There is a name for working this way, vibe coding, where the developer describes what they want in rough terms and lets the model fill in the rest. Developers now spend more of the day watching that than typing.Every one of those loops is billed, and they do not add up in a straight line, because each attempt drags along everything the agent read before it. Ten tries cost more than ten times one try. A flat monthly fee used to absorb that. This year nearly every major coding tool switched to charging for what gets used, and the sums became the developer's problem.Darko Mesaros has spent much of the past year arguing developers off that habit. A distinguished developer advocate at AWS, he spends his week in front of developers, explaining how the company's tools work and building with them himself. The tool is Kiro, the development environment Amazon launched a year ago, designed around the opposite instinct: settle a written specification first, argue it out line by line, and generate nothing until the document is agreed.Amazon calls this spec-driven development, and Mesaros says the time it takes upfront is why he rarely has to redo work. "When I build something with spec-driven development, I can usually one-shot things," he said. "Even though it's a bigger lift initially, it can literally one-shot things instead of iterating over multiple loops and costing many tokens."The billing shift behind that argument happened fast. OpenAI moved Codex to token-based credits in April, GitHub Copilot followed in June, and Cursor ended its flat-rate pricing in August, a month after launching an India-only plan at Rs 649.Claude Code now runs a weekly cap over a rolling five-hour limit.The price per token is not the reason. The same capability costs less every few months, and Anthropic has held Sonnet 5 at two dollars per million input tokens after dropping a planned increase in August. What grew is the work behind a single instruction, since an agent that opens a repository, writes a file, runs the tests and tries again spends tokens on every cycle, and the context it carries grows as it goes.Providers have a partial fix, called prompt caching. A model stores the unchanged opening portion of a request and reads it back later at a tenth of the normal input price. It only works if that portion is identical, character for character, so a timestamp near the top of a prompt or a model swapped mid-task will break it. Nothing flags that, and teams find out from the invoice.So one team can pay ten times what another pays for identical work. Three things decide it: which model picks up the job, how many attempts it takes, and how much of the context can be read from cache. Kiro goes after all three.Start with the attempts. A Kiro spec is three files the tool drafts and the developer approves before any code exists. The requirements file lists user stories in EARS notation, a format from safety-critical engineering where every line is a condition and a response: when a user submits a form with invalid data, the system shall show errors next to the relevant fields. The design file sets out the architecture, and the tasks file breaks the build into steps that run in parallel.Mesaros puts the weight on the approval, not the drafting. "When I'm certain on the spec and we go through all the things and I agree on all the things modified, it takes that spec," he said. Changing direction while the requirements are open costs an edited line, where the same change after generation means another full pass over the codebase.Model choice goes to a router Kiro calls the auto model, which sits in front of a catalogue spanning Anthropic, OpenAI and open-weight models, reads the prompt and decides what should handle it. "If the task is super simple, it's probably going to use the smaller model, which is a lot faster," Mesaros said. "But if it's something more complex, it's going to choose accordingly."He is careful to say the router works on complexity, with the cost following close behind. Running a task on Sonnet 4.6 instead costs about 1.3 times as many of Kiro's credits for the same work. The router also picks once, at the start of a task, and stays with it, which keeps the cache intact.Context is loaded the same way. Memory and lessons come in once, when a session opens, and each turn after refreshes only the project rules and short references to relevant skills. Mesaros points to the semantic memory underneath, a vector database the agent queries instead of reloading instruction files wholesale, which he calls the more optimised route.AWS says the homegrown trading platform Dhan built a real-time charting system supporting more than 170 indicators in eight weeks with one engineer, against an estimate of 12 to 24 months. Glimmertech, another customer, credits the structure with catching what it calls Potemkin house problems, where code looks finished but does not work underneath. Both accounts come from Amazon and are unverified.Nor does Amazon claim any of it comes free. Its own guide calls this an engineering investment and warns the first few weeks feel slower. Everyone else is arriving at some version of the idea anyway, since Claude Code reads a CLAUDE.md file into every request, Codex reads AGENTS.md and Cursor supports rules files.None of it is new either. Writing the requirements before the code is what software engineering did for decades, until it came to look like an expensive way to be slow. EARS came out of aircraft and medical devices, where finding out later was never an option.What has changed is who the document is for. For decades it was written for whichever engineer inherited the project two years on, and it was the first thing dropped when a deadline arrived. Now a machine reads it at the start of every session, and every reading turns up on the bill. Developers let the specification go because it felt like a slow way to work, and the billing is why Mesaros thinks it is coming back.
Article Summary: Amazon's Kiro lets AI agents write code, run tests and try again. But each attempt drags along everything the agent read before it. Ten tries cost more than ten times one try. Developers now spend more of the day watching that than typing.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Fei Fei Li: Smart CEOs should be thinking about AI and its impact on their respective business
Article Text:
Quote of the day

Smart CEOs should be thinking about AI and its impact on their respective business. Fei-Fei Li- Godmother of AI

What the quote actually means

Where can AI make the biggest difference

How could AI change customer expectations

What parts of the business could be automated

What new products or services could AI enable

What are the risks

How will employees work with AI

What are competitors doing

How should AI fit into the

business strategy

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way businesses operate. It affects everything from how companies interact with customers to how employees perform everyday tasks. As AI becomes part of more products, services, and business processes, companies increasingly have to consider how the technology could affect their operations and plans.That is the idea behind a quote by Fei-Fei Li, the computer scientist and AI researcher, who said: “Smart CEOs should be thinking about AI and its impact on their respective business.” Li, who is widely known as the “Godmother of AI”, has been one of the prominent voices in the development of modern AI and computer vision. The statement highlights that understanding AI is becoming an important part of thinking about a business's future.Li's statement is closely tied to how businesses should approach technological change. AI is not simply another technology that companies can consider separately from their existing operations. Depending on the industry, it can influence how products are developed, how decisions are made, how employees work and how customers interact with a company.Thinking about AI's impact does not mean every business needs to introduce AI into every part of its operations immediately. Instead, it means understanding where the technology could create opportunities, where it could introduce risks and how it could change the competitive landscape.For example, a company may use AI to automate repetitive tasks, analyse large amounts of data or improve customer support. At the same time, it may need to consider questions around accuracy, privacy, security, costs and how employees will work alongside AI systems.Some questions that can help CEOs think about AI's impact include:Identifying areas where AI can improve existing processes can help companies focus their efforts rather than adopting the technology simply because it is available.As people become familiar with AI-powered products and services, their expectations around speed, personalisation and convenience may also change.AI can handle or assist with some repetitive tasks, potentially allowing employees to spend more time on work that requires creativity, judgement and human interaction.AI can create opportunities that may not have been possible with earlier technologies, potentially changing what a company can offer its customers.Businesses also need to consider issues such as incorrect AI-generated information, data privacy, cybersecurity, intellectual property and the reliability of AI systems.AI's impact isn't limited to technology teams. Companies may need to rethink workflows, training and the skills employees need as AI becomes part of everyday work.Understanding how other companies are experimenting with AI can provide a broader view of how the technology may be changing an industry.AI initiatives are more useful when connected to a company's actual priorities rather than treated as separate technology projects.Businesses can easily view AI as a technology trend and wait to see how it develops. But AI's impact can extend beyond individual tools or features. It can affect how companies build products, compete for customers and organise their workforce.That is where Li's statement becomes relevant. Thinking about AI does not necessarily mean predicting exactly what the technology will look like several years from now. It means considering how current developments could affect a company's business and preparing for different possibilities.The same approach can apply to businesses of different sizes. A large company may be considering how AI can change its existing products and operations, while a smaller business may be looking at whether AI tools can help it compete with larger organisations.For CEOs, the discussion is therefore not limited to asking, “Should we use AI?” It can also involve asking, “Where could AI change our business, what opportunities could it create, and what do we need to prepare for?”AI can also change the nature of competition. If a technology allows companies to perform certain tasks faster or develop new services, businesses that understand those changes may need to rethink how they operate. At the same time, companies must balance experimentation with practical considerations such as costs, reliability, and responsible use.The idea also changes the way business leaders approach technological change. Instead of treating AI as something that belongs only to the technology department, the conversation becomes broader: “How could AI affect our customers, employees, products, competitors and business model?”That shift can help companies see AI not simply as a new technology, but as a factor that could shape how their business develops in the years ahead.
Article Summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way businesses operate. It affects everything from how companies interact with customers to how employees perform everyday tasks. As AI becomes part of more products, services, and business processes, companies increasingly have to consider how the technology could affect their operations.

Article Title: Sekyo launched AI-powered kids smartwatch Neo Fit in India, priced at Rs 9,990
Article Text:
Price and availability

Neo Fit Kids smartwatch features

Sekyo, India’s smart lifestyle technology brand, has unveiled Neo Fit, the country’s first AI-powered kids smartwatch equipped with health sensors. Designed to meet the evolving needs of children and parents, Neo Fit combines AI learning assistance, health monitoring, GPS tracking, communication tools, and parental controls in one wearable device.The Neo Fit Kids Smartwatch is priced at Rs 9,990 and is available through Sekyo’s official website, Amazon, Flipkart, and other e-commerce partners. The product comes with free shipping and a one-year warranty, making it accessible for families seeking a safe and connected alternative to smartphones for children.At its core, Neo Fit introduces an AI Learning Coach that provides study assistance through voice and image recognition, alongside seven educational and mathematics games. The smartwatch also tracks key health metrics including heart rate, SpO2, sleep, steps, and activity levels, while offering smart reminders for everyday habits like homework and reading.Neo Fit integrates real-time GPS tracking, geo-fencing, and route history to ensure child safety. For communication, it supports 4G video calling, WhatsApp calling and chat, and SOS alerts with live location sharing. Parents can manage the device through the Sekyo parental-control app, which also includes a “Find My Watch” feature.Built for everyday use, Neo Fit features:•2GB RAM and 32GB storage•2-inch HD display•Front camera and pedometer•IP67 water resistance•Available in Blue, Grey, and Pink color variantsSmridhi Goyal, CEO & Co-Founder of Sekyo, said: “Neo Fit is our vision of what a kids’ smartwatch can become when technology is designed around the real needs of children and parents. It supports smart AI learning, encourages healthy habits, enhances safety, and keeps families connected — without the distractions of a smartphone.”

Article Title: US Immigration authority has 10-day deadline on home address; says: You are responsible for keeping your …
Article Text:
US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)

How to change your address with USCIS

How to change your address with USCIS online

How to change your address with USCIS by mail

US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has a reminder for immigrants in the country asking them to report a change of address to the agency within 10 days of moving, warning that failing to update the address could lead to missed notices, delays in immigration cases and problems receiving immigration documents. The immigration authority shared the reminder on X (formerly Twitter), also making clear that changing an address with the US Postal Service does not automatically update records with USCIS.“Changing your address with USPS does not update your address with USCIS, and USPS will not forward USCIS mail. You are responsible for keeping your address current with both USCIS and USPS. If you do not update your address with USCIS, you may miss notices, your case may be delayed, and you may not receive your immigration documents,” the agency wrote.The post also has a link to the USCIS webpage detailing the process of address change. Here’s what it saysIf you have filed an immigration benefit request with USCIS, you must notify USCIS of any changes of address as soon as possible to ensure you receive all correspondence and benefits without delay. Additionally, all aliens in the United States must report a change of address to USCIS within 10 days of moving. This reporting requirement does not apply to A and G visa holders and visa waiver visitors.We strongly encourage you to submit your change of address through a USCIS online account as soon as you move.Changing your address with the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) will not change your address with USCIS and USPS will not forward your mail from USCIS. Please update your information with both USCIS and USPS. We recommend you use the USPS Look Up a ZIP Code tool to ensure that you give USCIS your full address using the standard abbreviations and formatting recognized by USPS.Using an online account to update your address in a timely way meets the legal requirement to notify us that you have moved. It also ensures that your case will continue processing without interruption and that you receive all correspondence and benefits without delay. Changing your address online allows us to process your change of address almost immediately and eliminates the need to file a paper Form AR-11, Alien’s Change of Address Card, by mail.Most people can change their address online using the USCIS Enterprise Change of Address (E-COA) self-service change-of-address tool. This tool can be found in their USCIS Online Account under the My Account dropdown menu. If you do not have a USCIS online account, see our How to Create a USCIS Online Account page. Some people may not have access to this feature, see the Specific Procedures for Certain Populations section for more information.If you have a pending, approved, or previously filed case with USCIS, you may change your address using your USCIS online account even if you initially filed your benefit request by mail.NOTE: If you use your USCIS online account to change your address, you must enter the receipt numbers for each pending benefit request to apply the address change. Providing receipt numbers helps ensure that we update your address where needed and that you continue to receive important correspondence and benefits related to these cases from USCIS without delay.USCIS says applicants with pending, approved, or previously filed cases can submit an address change through their online account, even if they originally filed the immigration benefit request by mail, simplifying the update process.You also may file a paper Form AR-11 by mail to change your address. This meets the legal requirement to notify USCIS of a change of address. However, because filing a paper-based Form AR-11 does not provide for an automated update to your address in USCIS systems, we strongly encourage requestors to use the self-service change of address tool available in their USCIS online account when reporting a change of address.
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has a reminder for immigrants in the country asking them to report a change of address to the agency within 10 days of moving. The immigration authority shared the reminder on X (formerly Twitter), also making clear that changing an address with the US Postal Service does not automatically update records with USCIS.

Article Title: Google engineer quits his "amazing" job over AI, and says the doomers have it wrong: I am not convinced the chance of ASI doom is…
Article Text:
Google DeepMind engineer says his chip design work was speeding up AI

This AI safety resignation stops short of predicting doom

O'Callahan plans to keep working on AI after leaving Google

Robert O'Callahan, a Google DeepMind engineer based in Auckland, has resigned over how fast artificial intelligence is advancing. In a resignation email shared on his blog this week, he wrote that AI progress is "far too rapid". His team's goal of making AI "much cheaper and lower-latency", he added, was not good for people right now.Yet O'Callahan stops short of the extinction warnings that have dominated the AI debate this month. He wrote that he is "not convinced the chance of ASI doom is 100%", referring to artificial superintelligence. The risk, in his view, is "real but uncertain". That alone, he argued, makes chasing ASI in the near future "inherently irresponsible".O'Callahan did not build AI models himself. He worked on tools for hardware chip design. For a while, he wrote, he told himself the work was relatively harmless. Over time he came to accept that its main impact would be faster design of a new breed of AI chips, making AI cheaper, faster and more capable.His exit lands in the same week Google laid out plans to test its AI chips in space. Under Project Suncatcher, a prototype satellite carrying Google's Trillium TPUs will fly on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission.The satellite was built with Earth imaging company Planet. The long-term goal is to see whether orbit could host AI data centres, since solar panels there can generate up to eight times more power than on Earth. "One small step for TPUs...," CEO Sundar Pichai posted on X. O'Callahan's post does not mention the project.Leaving was not easy. He said being "paid handsomely to solve fun puzzles" had been amazing. Moving teams was impractical too, since Google has no other engineering teams in New Zealand. A Christian and a church elder in Auckland, he wrote that ignoring his work's impact "would not be a Jesus-following thing to do".He joins a string of researchers who have left top AI labs over safety fears. Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic earlier this month, later warning in an interview that "we could all die" if development did not slow down. Former Google DeepMind researchers Rishub Jain and Bilal Chughtai also left this year.Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has since proposed slowing frontier AI development, with Sam Altman, Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk backing him publicly. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back, calling extinction warnings "doomsday narratives".O'Callahan sits somewhere between the two camps. He wrote that several doomer predictions, including reward hacking, misalignment and deceptive models, have already come true. But he has seen no hard evidence that insiders are hyping AI risk to lift stock prices or shut out rivals. Regulation, in his words, is "desperately needed".He admitted his exit will have a very small impact, "but not no impact; some of my skills are rare". The timing, he said, has nothing to do with the recent wave of viral resignations. He had picked the date long ago, ahead of a ten-day backpacking trip with friends on New Zealand's Abel Tasman and Wangapeka tracks.He is not walking away from AI altogether. O'Callahan will keep maintaining the debugging tools rr and Pernosco, and plans to study how AI agents debug code. He wants his next project to be "unambiguously pro-human".
Article Summary: Robert O'Callahan, a Google DeepMind engineer based in Auckland, has resigned over how fast artificial intelligence is advancing. In a resignation email shared on his blog this week, he wrote that AI progress is "far too rapid" His team's goal of making AI "much cheaper and lower-latency", he added, was not good for people right now.

Article Title: Meta AI CEO Alexandr Wang sets the record straight on how he dressed for Meta's Connect 2026 conference this week; says: Excuse me I must ...
Article Text:
Alexandr Wang corrects the record

Alexandr Wang’s camouflage shirt has become part of his usual style

Meta AI CEO Alexandr Wang recently made headlines for his outfit onto the Meta Connect stage. Rather than a polished tech suit, the tech CEO wore a deer-print camouflage T-shirt, dark trousers and camouflage Crocs. While many criticised Wang’s his casual wear, others started doing a fashion price check. A post on X (formerly known as Twitter) allegedly claimed that Alexandr Wang was actually wearing a £600 ($800) Hermès 'hunter classic shirt', £900 ($1,200) Loro Piana trousers and £1,125 ($1,500) Ferragamo shoes. Put together, the outfit supposedly cost £2,625 ($3,500). Wang was quick to “correct the record”.Responding to the post by X user Goltra @Goltra, the Meta’s AI chief said: “excuse me I must correct the record on this slander”. He also shared an annotated photo correcting the record with actual prices: $30 thrifted camo tee, $150 Norrona cargo pants, $60 Realtree Crocs, and hair from "putting his head in a washing machine".In another playful reply to a compliment on his improved fitness to a similar post, Wang wrote: “actually if you say i look fit i don’t care how much you lie about how much my clothes cost”.The shirt worn by Alexandr Wang appears to be a vintage-style camouflage top with deer prints on the front and “Lake Tahoe” printed on the sleeve.Similar 1990s “Back to Earth” shirts have been listed on the second-hand market for £11 to £34 ($14 to $45). However, the exact brand of Wang’s shirt has not been independently confirmed.“Meta AI keynote @alexandr_wang fit check: vintage deer tee, technical pants, camo Crocs. Estimated damage: $264–$294,” said an X post. Wang confirmed the same writing “yes this is all correct thank you Boys Club World”.Notably,. Alexandr Wang’s casual style is also not new. He has worn deer-print and camouflage shirts during interviews and important work meetings in the past. The outfit at Meta Connect therefore appears to be part of his regular style rather than a one-time choice for the event.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang’s camouflage shirt has become part of his usual style. He has worn deer-print and camouflage shirts during interviews and important work meetings in the past. The outfit at Meta Connect appears to be a regular choice rather than a one-time choice.

Article Title: Microsoft launches new Copilot with AI agents, Office tools and a new Code feature: Here’s everything you need to know
Article Text:
Microsoft Copilot gets a new Home experience

Code lets users build apps and workflows

Autopilot can continue working on tasks

More business data and plugins

Microsoft updates Copilot AI spending controls

Microsoft has introduced a new version of Copilot. The latest version brings AI agents, Office tools and a new Code feature into a single experience. The tech giant is positioning the updated Copilot as a place where users can ask questions, delegate longer tasks, create documents and build small software solutions.The update adds three key capabilities: Home, Code and Autopilot. Home brings Chat and Cowork together, Office in Copilot adds Word, Excel and PowerPoint capabilities, while Code lets users create apps, dashboards and workflows using natural-language instructions. Meanwhile, Autopilot is designed to continue working on assigned tasks without requiring a new prompt each time.Microsoft has confirmed that Home will become Copilot's starting point, combining Chat and Cowork in one interface. Chat is designed for questions, lookups, and drafting, while Cowork handles multi-step tasks and produces a completed result.Microsoft said Copilot will eventually be able to determine whether a request should be handled by Chat, Cowork or Code, removing the need for users to select a mode themselves.The company is also bringing Office capabilities directly into Copilot. Users will be able to create or update Word documents, Excel workbooks and PowerPoint presentations from the Copilot interface.Files remain editable and can stay synchronised with the corresponding Microsoft 365 applications.The new Code feature aims to let non-developers create small, purpose-built software solutions. Users can describe an app, tracker, dashboard, automation or workflow in natural language, after which Copilot builds it.Microsoft said Code uses the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot and operates in a sandboxed environment. Solutions can include desktop widgets, interactive dashboards and cloud-hosted internal applications.Code is scheduled to enter Microsoft's Frontier programme at the end of the month, with broader availability planned in the following weeks. A preview will also be available to Microsoft 365 Premium and Pro subscribers later this year.Microsoft is also introducing Copilot Managed Runtime, a hosting environment that lets applications created through Code, Cowork, and Copilot Studio run within an organisation's Microsoft 365 environment.Autopilot, previously known as Scout, is Microsoft's persistent agent designed to continue working after a user assigns it a goal. Users can give Autopilot a name, role and objective, after which it can monitor channels, follow up on conversations and handle recurring work. The agent operates in the cloud and has its own identity, memory, computer and workspace within the organisation's tenant.Microsoft said Autopilot is designed to work across Teams, Outlook, chats, channels and documents, while remaining subject to permissions, auditing and organisational controls. Autopilot will expand to private preview at the end of September.Microsoft is expanding Copilot's access to business context through Microsoft IQ. Fabric IQ brings data from Power BI semantic models into Copilot, while integration with Dynamics 365 and Power Platform is planned for public preview.A new plugin registry will also bring Microsoft, partner and custom-built plugins into one catalogue. Administrators can approve and manage plugins centrally.Microsoft is also adding FinOps capabilities for managing AI spending. The company is separating everyday Copilot use from longer-running agentic workloads.A user subscription license covers Copilot across applications such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams. Usage-based billing applies to features including Cowork, Code and Autopilot.New administrative controls will let organisations manage spending policies, model availability, and credit requests. Users will also be able to see their credit usage, remaining balances and usage history within Copilot.Home and Code will begin rolling out through Microsoft's Frontier programme, while Autopilot is moving to private preview. Microsoft said it will continue rolling out additional Copilot features over the coming months.
Article Summary: Home brings Chat and Cowork together, Office in Copilot adds Word, Excel and PowerPoint capabilities. Code lets users create apps, dashboards and workflows using natural-language instructions. Autopilot is designed to continue working on assigned tasks without requiring a new prompt each time.
